title: Reading Triangle Correspondence
summary: Learn how the order of triangle names determines every corresponding vertex, side, and angle before using a triangle congruence test.
statusText: This guide explains notation and correspondence. It does not prove that a pair of triangles is congruent.
statementLatex: \text{If }\triangle ABC \cong \triangle EFD,\ \text{ then }A\leftrightarrow E,\;B\leftrightarrow F,\;C\leftrightarrow D.
learningObjectives: Read an ordered triangle-congruence statement from left to right.
Recover every corresponding vertex, side, and angle from that order.
Write a valid correspondence statement from a marked diagram.
Treat matching diagram marks as given information rather than estimating from the picture.
Distinguish congruent geometric objects from equal numerical values.
Recognize that screen position and orientation do not determine correspondence.

sections.title: Names carry an order
paragraphs: In △ABC ≅ △EFD, the first letters correspond, the second letters correspond, and the third letters correspond. Therefore A pairs with E, B pairs with F, and C pairs with D.
The order is part of the statement. Rearranging the same three letters can assert a different triangle correspondence.

sections.title: Read markings as given information
paragraphs: Matching side numbers, hatch marks, or angle arcs state which parts are paired. They are given facts from the diagram, not estimates based on how the picture looks.
Unmarked parts must not be assumed congruent merely because they look alike.

sections.title: Derive every corresponding part
paragraphs: Once the vertices are paired, the sides follow from their endpoints. If A pairs with E and B pairs with F, then side AB pairs with side EF.
Angles follow directly from their vertices: ∠A pairs with ∠E, ∠B with ∠F, and ∠C with ∠D.

sections.title: Read congruence notation precisely
paragraphs: Use ≅ for congruent geometric objects. Use = for numerical values after the notation has already told you that a symbol stands for a length or an angle size.
After triangle congruence is established, all corresponding sides and angles are congruent. This is often abbreviated CPCTC: corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent.

sections.title: Repair an invalid ordering
paragraphs: Check a proposed statement one position at a time. The first mismatch already makes the ordering invalid, even if another pair happens to match.
Use the exercise to test all six possible orders of D, E, and F against the marked correspondence.

sections.title: Correspondence is not appearance
paragraphs: Rotating or reflecting a triangle changes its appearance, not its labels or stated vertex correspondence.
A diagram illustrates the given relationships; its screen position does not prove that two triangles are congruent.

supplementalSections.title: Use the same correspondence for similar triangles
paragraphs: This section is reserved for the similarity unit. It will reuse the same ordered vertex rule and add consistent side-ratio direction only after similarity has been defined.
